2026.10 TDL Trend Report

The Next 5 Years of Logistics
through DHL’s Trend Radar 6.0 → 7.0 → 8.0: robots and AI are moving toward ‘connection’

Every two years, DHL maps the trends that will reshape logistics in its Logistics Trend Radar. This issue traces the shift from 6.0 (2022) to 8.0 (2026), shows where our automation areas stand today, and looks at the next five years.

6.0 · 20227.0 · 20248.0 · 2026 · 37 TRENDS
CH.1WHAT IS THE TREND RADAR

What Is the Trend Radar?

It is a map of logistics trends that DHL publishes every two years. It picks the social, business and technology trends that will reshape logistics and shows on one page how much (impact) and how soon (time to adoption) each one will change the industry.

WHO

Who makes it

The Trend Research team at DHL Customer Solutions & Innovation. It brings together input from customers, startups, technology providers, academia and experts.

WHEN

How often

Every two years. 8.0, published in September 2026, is the eighth edition. 6.0 (2022) → 7.0 (2024) → 8.0 (2026).

WHY

Why it exists

To separate lasting signals from short-lived hype and judge where value will be created. DHL uses it to run PoCs in real operations and scales the ones that work.

WHAT

What’s inside

Each trend gets an impact rating (4 levels), a time to adoption and an action label, plus a definition, real use cases, challenges and an outlook.

WHY IT MATTERSIt is the shared map of the logistics future that DHL uses with its customers and partners. It signals where DHL will invest next. For us, it is the benchmark for reading DHL’s direction and finding where we can get ahead.

CH.28.0 CORE MESSAGES

Four Key Messages of 8.0

Boil the 37 trends down and four words remain. Remember these four, and you understand 8.0.

01Agentic AI · HIGH · NEW
AI
Moves beyond analysis to act on its own

New entry Agentic AI is rated HIGH, while Generative AI is MODERATE. The reason is the ‘Gen AI paradox’: about 80% of companies use generative AI, yet a similar share see no bottom-line impact. Humanoids, AI with a body, are also new.

022030 · up to 30% of DHL MHE
Robots
Time to set the strategy now

Indoor Mobile Robots (HIGH) and Stationary Robotics (CONSIDERABLE) both carry the ‘Strategize’ label. DHL expects up to 30% of its material handling equipment to use robotic automation by 2030.

03Augmented Workplaces
People
Still at the center

Workforce Focus became Augmented Workplaces, and DEIB became Employee Belonging. Machines take the repetitive work. People handle judgment, exceptions and improvement.

045 of 12 HIGH
Sustainability
The biggest structural shift

Five of the 12 HIGH trends are Decarbonization, Sustainable Fuels, Circularity, Heavy Vehicle Electrification and Renewable Energy Infrastructure. Even amid the AI boom, these are rated as the changes that will reshape logistics the most.

CH.4AUTOMATION AREAS · PROGRESS

Five Automation Areas — Where They Stand Today

We group the automation areas LX Pantos focuses on into five: Mobile Robot · Robot Arm · AI · Digital Twin · New Mobility. Humanoids are treated as AI with a body (Physical AI) and placed under AI. All five are already active in the field. What differs is how far each one has come.

AREA
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
CURRENT STAGE · PROGRESS
Mobile RobotIndoor Mobile Robots
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
SCALING1 billion cumulative picks across 40+ DHL sites. The truck-unloading robot Stretch was first deployed commercially in 2023.
Robot ArmStationary Robotics
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
EARLY COMMERCIALRunning in induction, palletizing and automated storage. Successful pilots are growing ahead of a large-scale rollout.
AIAgentic AI · AI Analytics · Computer Vision · Humanoids
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
EARLY COMMERCIALAgents have moved past pilots into dock scheduling, driver calls and customs guidance. Vision has matured greatly in the last two years. Humanoids (Physical AI) are being piloted on repetitive tasks, and H1 2026 investment of US$4.39B already exceeds all of 2025.
Digital TwinDigital Twins
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
EARLY COMMERCIALMoving from monitoring to real action. Low-code tools and AI agents are lowering the barrier to entry: a ‘tipping point’.
New MobilityAutonomous driving · e-vans · drones
PilotEarly commercialScalingMainstream
EARLY COMMERCIALStarting in controlled zones: 70 autonomous vehicles at Hong Kong airport and 10 autonomous electric trucks at a port in Guangdong.

Stages are this report’s judgment based on the DHL Logistics Trend Radar 8.0 text · Pilot → Early commercial → Scaling → Mainstream

Applications and next challenges by areaFIVE AREAS

AREA 01 · SCALING

Mobile Robot

8.0 trend: Indoor Mobile Robots
APPLICATIONS
Inter-site transfer, AMR-assisted picking, autonomous forklifts, inventory scanning, mobile sorting
CASES
DHL: Stretch truck unloading; Locus Origin at 40+ sites with 1B cumulative picks
NEXT CHALLENGE
Unified control of multi-vendor robots; loading and unloading mixed cartons
AREA 02 · EARLY COMMERCIAL

Robot Arm

8.0 trend: Stationary Robotics
APPLICATIONS
Induction and singulation, uniform-carton (de)palletizing, automated storage, packing and labeling
CASES
DHL: robotic induction cell in Spain, cobot palletizing in Czechia, AutoStore
NEXT CHALLENGE
Handling mixed cartons; handoffs with mobile robots
AREA 03 · EARLY COMMERCIAL

AI

8.0 trends: Agentic AI · AI Analytics · Computer Vision · Humanoids
APPLICATIONS
Dock-scheduling and shipment-alert agents, demand and inventory forecasting, vision-based safety monitoring and dimensioning, humanoid pilots for repetitive tasks and patrols
CASES
DHL: HappyRobot agents (scheduling, driver calls), a customs-guidance call agent for US-bound shipments · Industry: Figure AI, Boston Dynamics and Unitree advancing humanoids
NEXT CHALLENGE
A shared cargo and customer data model, oversight of autonomous decisions, humanoid uptime and safety standards
AREA 04 · EARLY COMMERCIAL

Digital Twin

8.0 trend: Digital Twins
APPLICATIONS
Facility layout and workflow simulation, predictive maintenance, stress tests for supply chain disruptions
CASES
Industry: PepsiCo pre-validating layouts; Samsung Electronics’ manufacturing twin plus planned logistics AI agents
NEXT CHALLENGE
Data integration and interoperability, low-code tools, links to AI agents
AREA 05 · EARLY COMMERCIAL

New Mobility

8.0 trends: Outdoor Autonomous Vehicles · Vehicle Electrification · UAS
APPLICATIONS
Autonomous transfer at yards, airports and ports; urban e-vans; indoor drone inventory counts
CASES
DHL: autonomous baggage transport PoC at Heathrow (Oxa) · Industry: 70 autonomous vehicles at Hong Kong airport
NEXT CHALLENGE
Remote operations (one operator, many vehicles), V2X communication, long-haul autonomous freight
KEY POINTThe next challenge for all five areas is the same: connection — controlling many robots as one, letting robots hand goods to each other, and adding AI on top.

CH.5THE NEXT FIVE YEARS

The Next Five Years — Where the Momentum Goes

We expect the fields that connect technologies, rather than any single technology, to lead the next five years. The predictions below are this report’s interpretation, based on the outlook DHL 8.0 gives for each trend.

01

AI orchestration

Vision, analytics, digital twins and agents merge into one ‘sense–decide–act’ layer.

Basis: Agentic AI central over the next 5 years · twins become AI decision engines
02

Robot handoffs and unified control

Competition shifts from one robot’s performance to the ability to connect many robots.

Basis: ‘warehouse-wide orchestration’ · stationary↔mobile handoffs
03

Physical AI · Humanoids

Today they handle specific tasks. We expect a turning point toward general use around 2030.

Basis: H1 2026 investment US$4.39B > all of 2025 US$3.05B
04

Autonomy and remote ops in controlled zones

Unmanned operation will speed up first where boundaries are clear: yards, airports, ports and facility interiors.

Basis: controlled sites mature before public roads · remote ops widespread within 5 years
05

Edge, connectivity and power

On-site edge AI, seamless connectivity, and charging and grid capacity become the bottlenecks of automation.

Basis: edge AI in smart assets · satellite links · infrastructure sets the pace of electrification

Predictions are this report’s interpretation · Basis: the outlook for each trend in DHL Logistics Trend Radar 8.0

Our Solutions Today

CONCLUSION

Beyond Following — Getting Ahead

DHL does not stop at predicting trends. Its mobile robots run at more than 40 sites, and AI agents already handle customer service and operational coordination. If we follow the same path in the same order, the gap will not close.

Where we can get ahead is in the areas that even DHL still lists as its ‘next step’.

01

Scale the ‘Strategize now’ areas first

For Mobile Robot, Robot Arm and AI, start from the tasks DHL has already scaled, and design the path that takes each PoC to the next site at the same time.

02

Lead on connection

Robot-to-robot handoffs, unified control of multi-vendor robots and a ‘see–decide–act’ AI loop are still on DHL’s list of next steps.

03

Start Physical AI pilots now

Build experience with humanoids, part of the AI area, on repetitive tasks, so we can scale quickly once commercialization speeds up.

And at the center of all this change must be people who can work alongside new technology.

APPENDIXGLOSSARY
Logistics Trend Radar
A map of logistics trends published every two years by DHL Customer Solutions & Innovation. 6.0 (2022), 7.0 (2024), 8.0 (2026).
Impact
How strongly a trend will affect logistics. HIGH → CONSIDERABLE → MODERATE → LOW.
Adoption (time to adoption)
Time until a trend becomes ‘the common way of operating’ in logistics: under 5 years, or 5–10 years.
Strategize · Prepare · Explore · Consider
DHL’s action label for each trend: build it into strategy · build capabilities · explore use cases · keep watching.
Agentic AI
AI systems that take a goal and then perceive, decide, plan and act on their own. People take a supervisory role.
Physical AI
AI that perceives, understands, reasons about and acts in the physical world. The foundation for humanoids and autonomous robots.
Digital Twin
A virtual model that mirrors physical assets and processes in real time. Used for visualization, prediction, simulation and optimization.
Handoff
The point where one robot or machine sets down goods and the next one picks them up. Key to linking stationary and mobile robots.
Orchestration
Coordinating many robots, systems and tasks as one flow. Unified control of multi-vendor robots is a typical example.
Self-Healing Supply Chain
A supply chain that detects and diagnoses disruptions, responds within set guardrails and learns from the results.
Remote Operations
Operating and managing forklifts, yard trucks, warehouse robots and more without being on site.
V2X
Vehicle-to-Everything. Real-time data exchange between a vehicle and infrastructure, other vehicles and systems.

NOTICEABOUT THIS REPORT

This report summarizes and restructures the original DHL Logistics Trend Radar 8.0 (September 2026) and the press releases and public summaries of 6.0 and 7.0. Because the original 6.0 and 7.0 PDFs could not be reviewed, impact and adoption ratings are compared on an 8.0 basis only. Market sizes, investment amounts and other figures come from the original sources cited by DHL, and vendor figures are each company’s own claims. The radar has been redrawn to approximate the original layout. The trend themes, automation-area mapping, five-year predictions and conclusion are this report’s interpretation.
